extraction.name: The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation
extraction.description: The FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark consists of 3001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia and covering a variety of different topics and domains. These sentences have been translated in 101 languages by professional translators through a carefully controlled process. The resulting dataset enables better assessment of model quality on the long tail of low-resource languages, including the evaluation of many-to-many multilingual translation systems, as all translations are multilingually aligned. By publicly releasing such a high-quality and high-coverage dataset, it aims to foster progress in the machine translation community and beyond.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The overall construction process consisted of three phases: (i) extracting sentences to translate from English Wikipedia, (ii) designing and running pilot experiments to determine the translation process, and (iii) launching the actual translation workflow for over 100 languages. Sentences were translated by professional translators through a carefully controlled process, including automated quality control steps and human evaluation with re-translation rounds if quality was insufficient.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: All source sentences were extracted from multiple Wikimedia sources, specifically English Wikipedia, Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The sentence selection process involved manually selecting 3-5 contiguous sentences from randomly chosen articles from English Wikipedia, Wikinews, Wikijunior, and WikiVoyage. Sentences with very short or malformed structures were avoided. Paragraphs were balanced across article sections (beginning, middle, end). Metadata such as Wikipedia URL, topic, and boolean flags for linked entities and images were extracted. Sentences were manually labeled with one of 10 detailed sub-topics.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Sentences were translated by professional translators from Language Service Providers (LSPs). The workflow involved an initial LSP for translation and editing, followed by quality assurance (QA) performed by an independent LSP. Translations underwent automatic checks for language identification, source sentence copying, length differences, fluency (via language model), and copying from public translation engines. If automatic checks failed, translations were sent back for re-translation. Human evaluators from an independent LSP then performed quality assessment, calculating a Translation Quality Score (0-100%) based on errors in grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register (with minor, major, critical severities). A score below 90% triggered re-translation by the original LSP, with further human evaluation if the initial score was below a certain threshold.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translation quality was assessed through a Translation Quality Score, calculated per language on a 0 to 100 scale. This score was determined by tallying identified errors (grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition or omission of information, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register), each associated with a severity level (minor, major, critical). The acceptable translation quality score was set to 90%. Any set of translations with more than 10% of sentences violating automatic checks (e.g., copying from translation engines) required re-translation. The process could involve multiple rounds of human evaluation and re-translation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: For sentence selection: 10 annotators (6 male, 4 female) with roles as researchers (scientists and engineers) and program/project managers, originating from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Language identification tools, tools for checking source sentence copying, tools for checking significant length differences, language models for fluency checking, tools for checking copying from publicly available translation engines.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The test set will not be released publicly but will be available via a publicly available evaluation server. The dev and devtest sets are publicly downloadable. There is a hope to continue to expand the number of languages covered in FLORES-101 and make the test set available to various community efforts to improve translation systems in shared tasks.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to foster progress in the machine translation community and beyond, particularly for low-resource languages, by providing a reliable, high-quality evaluation benchmark. This is crucial for developing, iterating, and testing models and techniques to improve translation quality for languages spoken by the majority of the world's population.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset acknowledges a potential bias of 'translationese' (overly literal or awkward translations) due to sourcing from English Wikipedia and translating into other languages. However, the authors conjecture these effects are marginal for low-resource languages where current MT systems produce severe mistakes, and that the benefits of many-to-many evaluation outweigh this risk.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Several languages considered for inclusion were unable to meet the required 90% quality threshold after multiple rounds of re-translation and were therefore excluded. The largest observed error category across all languages was 'mistranslation', which includes incorrect interpretation of source text, literal translations, mistranslations of phrasal verbs, and lack of disambiguation of ambiguous terms. All domains proved challenging for human translators, with WikiVoyage being slightly harder due to more named entities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for evaluating machine translation model quality, especially for low-resource and many-to-many multilingual translation systems. It supports evaluation of 101x101 language pairs. With rich metadata, it also supports document-level translation, multimodal translation, and text classification. The dataset is split into dev (for hyper-parameter tuning), devtest (for development testing), and test (for evaluation via a public server to prevent overfitting and ensure equivalent assessment).
